correctness.rationale: Every perfect matching is a 15-position bijective incidence assignment, exhausted by recursion (288 cases). All 720 symbol permutations produce precisely two disjoint 144-element orbits. A complete superset zeta transform of 32768 subsets per representative computes each forcing count exactly. Independent full-vertex exact cover enumeration returns 288 matchings and direct tests confirm zero forcing four-subsets, 240 five-subsets per orbit, and 1380/1355 six-subsets. Full coefficients and the orbit transfer are reconstructed in RESULT.md and replayed by standalone programs.

value.rationale: Forcing subsets are natural identifying certificates for perfect matchings. The exact 5-edge threshold and complete polynomials quantify their availability in the smallest cubic girth-eight cage. Distinct six-edge counts 1380 and 1355 separate two natural symmetry classes that share the same ordinary forcing number, a structural refinement not supplied by the known 288-count.
